source.title: Dueling Deep Reinforcement Learning for Financial Time Series

record.file_problem: Full text is present; some figure captions are inconsistent, including captions that label both CNN test figures as without commission costs.
record.tranche_reason: Tests batch-size effects on trading rewards in financial time-series reinforcement learning, a new setting relative to the mapped generalization claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports test trading rewards by architecture, batch size, and commission condition. These are not supervised test errors or train–test gaps, and the study does not test memorization of random labels. Its results therefore fit none of the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares financial-trading rewards across batch sizes, architectures and commission conditions. These results do not test any listed version: V3 concerns image classification, and V5 concerns image classifiers or language models under fixed epoch budgets. Training lasts eight million steps; a separate held-out evaluation split is not specified.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors describe dueling DDQN as promising for trading and interpret the larger batches' resilience to commissions as suggesting more stable policies and better generalization. They acknowledge suboptimal policies and argue that more historical data and computation are needed. These are the authors' interpretations; the reported returns do not directly establish overfitting or a train–test generalization gap.
record.recipe_differences: Financial time-series trading with Double DQN and dueling feedforward or convolutional architectures; batch sizes and transaction costs are varied. The mapped sources concern supervised-learning generalization or other optimizer and regularization comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported trading returns vary with batch size, architecture, and whether commissions are included.

fits_no_version.finding: With commissions, increasing batch size from 32 to 128 changes reported annual returns from −35% to +8% for FFDQN and from −20% to +17% for CNN. Without commissions, returns change from +10% to +11% and from +20% to +16%, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this financial-trading experiment, batch-128 dueling DDQN agents achieve higher returns under transaction costs than batch-32 agents; without costs, the batch-size advantage depends on architecture.

record.problems: The study gives no uncertainty estimates. The text's reported CNN batch-128 return levels differ between Testing (exceeding 15% in both scenarios) and Conclusion (+16% and +17%). CNN figure captions incorrectly identify both commission conditions as without commission costs. No train–test error gap is measured.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out; the text reports aggregate annual returns for each architecture, batch size, and commission condition, and all eight combinations are included.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width beyond zero training error and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects on image-classification or language-model held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus randomly selected examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study discusses an original V5 source but incorrectly attributes difficulty generalizing with smaller batches to Keskar et al. This citation is not evidence against V5. No uncertainty estimates or clearly specified held-out split are provided. The record's claim that Testing and Conclusion disagree on CNN batch-128 returns is incorrect: +16% and +17% both exceed 15%.

Convolutional versus fully connected test error on image datasets.

Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
